neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: Generalizes the exact generators and cumulants to three circular ensembles, showing that logarithmic variance with bounded higher cumulants yields Gaussian real and imaginary parts in every symmetry class.

related_synthesis_entries.claim: Orthogonal, unitary, and symplectic models share logarithmic variance plus bounded higher cumulants, yet differ in variance constants, admissible rational moment subsequences, and pole/zero patterns.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: The shared Gaussian mechanism still requires class-specific calibration: symplectic and orthogonal ensembles alter both the logarithmic variance coefficient and its constant term.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: Using polygamma recurrence and separate sums, the source derives next-order variance asymptotics for CSE and COE, treats even and odd COE dimensions separately, and retains equality between real and imaginary second cumulants within each class.
directed.conceptual_reading: Symmetry affects the metric scale of fluctuations even when the normalized limiting shape is unchanged.
directed.representation_or_bridge: Integer and half-integer polygamma sums translate compact-group symmetry into explicit log N and constant contributions to the variance.
directed.boundary_or_failure: These calculations calibrate ensemble observables only; they neither justify a symmetry assignment for an L-function family nor make finite-N laws identical.
